coverage_prompt_rules: Treat each allowed intent as a daily-life API action, not a media or ML model task.

Use the requested real-world service domain to disambiguate similar actions: booking, buying, paying, applying, consulting, sending, sharing, searching, playing, calling, recording, printing, or setting reminders.

Cover an intent when the request asks to perform that service action even if the exact API name is not used, for example reserve/book, purchase/buy/order, pay/settle, call/contact, message/send, search/look up, or schedule/set.

Do not add adjacent service intents just because their entities appear. A hotel name does not imply book_hotel unless the request asks to reserve it; a restaurant name does not imply book_restaurant unless reservation or ordering is requested.
When one request contains multiple independent daily-life actions, return all independently covered intents, for example book flight plus book hotel plus order taxi.

Use required slot evidence from candidate tool descriptions to distinguish similar intents: date, location, destination, platform, product, recipient, content, doctor/lawyer/course/bank/company, or operation.
replan_prompt_rules: Prefer a direct API tool for each requested daily-life action.
Keep separate tools for separate service actions such as booking travel, booking lodging, ordering food, sending messages, and paying bills.
Do not insert media or ML-style preprocessing steps unless the allowed daily-life API explicitly requires them.
